characters.name: In General
characters.description: The Chosen One: Of their respective Triforce pieces — Link is always Courage, Zelda is always Wisdom, and Ganondorf is always Power. Ganondorf in particular is even granted the Triforce of Power in the Child Timeline when he's about to be executed inTwilight Princess, which the Sages see as a "divine prank". Chromatic Arrangement: Red, Blue, and Green for Ganondorf, Zelda, and Link, respectively. This is also the order of their Triforce arrangement, reading from the top, then left, then to the right. Divine Conflict:Skyward Swordreveals that while they use the powers of three Golden Goddesses, the conflict is ultimately derived from the battle between two specific lesser divine beings, the Goddess Hylia and Demon King Demise, and the mortal chosen as the former's champion. Hereditary Curse: Ganondorf, or something else controlling the Moblin and demon forces,willappear in every era that Zelda and Link reincarnate in just to cause trouble for them. At the same time, those two are the only people that can defeat him, and it's implied byinvokedMiyamotoit may in fact be the other way around: Zelda and Link only reincarnate when evil returns to threaten Hyrule.Skyward Swordspells out the reason for at least one of these problems:Ganondorf is the product of the curse of Demise destined to plague Link and Zelda's descendants. Humans by Any Other Name: Link and Zelda are Hylians, while Ganondorf is a Gerudo. Apart from thePointy Ears(which Ganondorf didn't even originally have), both races are virtually indistinguishable from real-life humans in appearance.

characters.name: Link
characters.description: The Ace: He is a powerful swordsman, (sometimes) a strong magic user, a skilled adventurer, and a legendary hero whose incarnations unfailingly appear across the centuries. Action Hero: Since he is a warrior, this is a given. Adorably Precocious Child: Even in his younger incarnations, Link is righteous and unbreakable. All-Loving Hero: Linkwillhelp those around him, no matter what. Affiliation, race, and different dimension mean little to him. To him, helping is helping. This is quite possiblywhyhe's the chosen of the Triforce Of Courage. It takes true courage to be willing to help so many people without a second thought for your safety. Alternate Self: The events ofOcarina of Timesplit the timeline in three, making the Links seen in the Decline, Adult, and Child timelines this to each other.He also has a cowardly Lorule counterpart named Ravio.

characters.name: Zelda
characters.description: One Head Taller: She has always been either taller than Link or the same height. One-Steve Limit: Averted. Like Link, therearemultiple Zeldas throughout the timeline, though for various reasons. For example, inThe Adventure of Link, it's explained that the prince mandated that every princess born be named Zelda in honor of his sister who was put to sleep defending the Triforce of Courage, and King Rhoam's diary inBreath of the Wildindicates that there is a less stringent tradition of naming princesses Zelda regardless of timeline. Achilles' Heel: While all Zeldas appear to have a degree to independence and even some have their own individual combat prowess thanks to their archery skills and light magic, a common weakness of every Zelda is their inability to deal with prolonged or powerful attack by herself. This usually leads them to their trouble and leads to the Link of their eras having to either help or rescue them. Action Girl: Some incarnations of Zelda are more willing to use their fists and swords rather than magic. These include thePirate GirlTetra and her descendant, Princess Zelda fromSpirit Tracks. Artifact Name: Certain titles such asTwilight PrincessorA Link Between Worldsstill call herPrincessZelda, even though she's the reigning monarch and should logically beQueenZelda instead.

characters.name: Ganon
characters.description: The Ganons of the "Wild Saga" can be foundhere(Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity),hereorhere(The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the WildandThe Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom) Other incarnations of Ganon can be found at their respective games' character pages. Achilles' Heel: The Master Sword is typically this, it's not called the "Blade of Evil's Bane" for nothing. InThe Legend of Zelda IandThe Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past, Silver Arrows are needed to finish him off. Affably Evil:Occasionally, Ganondorf is genuinely polite and respectful towards Link, viewing him as aWorthy Opponentand speaking to him as an equal. This is particularly pronounced inA Link to the PastandThe Wind Waker, where he has mellowed out following his initial defeat and is (somewhat) willing to put aside his pride to compliment his nemesis. Alas, Poor Villain: The defeats of his original incarnation are sometimes played somberly:After seemingly being defeated at the end ofOcarina of Time, Zelda laments how Ganondorf's hubris led to his own downfall.Zelda:Ganondorf…pitiful man… Without a strong, righteous mind, he could not control the power of the gods…and…The entire climax ofThe Wind Wakerserves as this for him, as he laments hisDark and Troubled Pastand prepares to finally accomplish his life's goal of claiming the Triforce…only for the King of Hyrule to reach it first, crushing his hopes and sending him spiraling into maniacal laughter. In his final breath, he takes a moment to feel Hyrule's wind— the wind that he coveted so desperately his entire life— on his face one last time before beingKilled Off for Real. Even the King of Hyrule expresses sympathy for Ganondorf's fate.King Daphnes:If only I could do things over again… Not a day of my life has gone by without my thoughts turning to my kingdom of old. I have lived bound to Hyrule. In that sense,I was the same as Ganondorf.After he dies at the end ofTwilight Princess, still refusing to give up on the hatred for Hyrule that consum

characters.name: Goddesses as a Group
characters.description: The divine creators of Hyrule, Din, Nayru, and Farore. In ancient times, they descended to the chaos that was the world at the time, created the known world and the creatures within it, and then departed, leaving the Triforce at the point in the world they left it. The Goddesses themselves almost never appear in aZeldatitle outside of flashbacks to their creation of the world, but creatures named for them and artifacts bearing their power frequently appear. All There in the Manual: They were first mentioned in the manual forA Link to the Past, but they wouldn't be portrayed in the actual games untilOcarina of Time, and didn't get a speaking role untilEchoes of Wisdom. Arch-Enemy: Their collective greatest opposition is Null, the very embodiment of thevoid before creation. Despite specks of existence spontaneously forming, Null saw it fit to devour them as it feels only it has the right to exist by its nature. The Golden Goddesses then created the Light World and Triforce to seal Null away ina small remnant of its void, and Null has endlessly plotted to return creation to nothing ever since. The Artifact: The fact that late in the series they're still being referred asGoldenGoddesses, despite the color gold having a much stronger association with Hylia. This comes from how all three of them were depicted as blondes (or "golden haired") inA Link to the Pastand as beings of pure gold wreathed in red (Din), blue (Nayru), and green (Farore) auras inOcarina of Time, but in later games, they're mostly associated with red (Din), blue (Nayru) and green (Farore) with no gold to be seen. Chromatic Arrangement: They're associated with the three additive primaries: Din is associated with red, Nayru is blue, and Farore is green.

characters.name: Din
characters.description: Din is the titular character ofOracle of Seasons, and shares the same name as the Goddess of Power. She holds the four seasons of Holodrum in their balance while in working in disguise as a popular dancer. Aborted Declaration of Love: One of her troupe members hints at her attraction to Link, but despite her outgoing nature otherwise, she ends up shying out of her one attempt at telling him herself. All Your Powers Combined: In the ending of a Linked Game, she combines her power with Nayru's to help Link reach theRoom of Rites. Ambiguously Brown: She has unusually dark skin for a Hylian, which is the reason why some people theorize that she's part Gerudo. Chained to a Rock: She's briefly subjected to this right after she gets captured, just long enough for Onox toexposit his evil plan.

characters.name: Nayru
characters.description: Goddess of Wisdom, represented by water and time, the color blue, and the Zora race. After Din created the land of Hyrule, Nayru breathed her wisdom onto it, creating the laws of space-time, and all other form of natural law. Blue Means Smart One: Nayru is the Goddess of Wisdom who created the laws of the world, and she is associated with the color blue. Deflector Shields: The spell associated with her, Nayru's Love, creates an energy barrier to protect the user. Ear Fins: Her statue inThe Wind Wakerdepicts her with webbed fins instead of ears, matching her association with water and the Zora people. Ethnic Goddess: She is associated with the Zora, an aquatic race with a complex social structure associated with the color blue. The fact that they are described as particularly close to the Royal Family of Hyrule, whose most prominent member, Princess Zelda, is the wielder of Nayru's Triforce of Wisdom, is also significant. There are also indications that the Sheikah, a similarly wise,Long-LivedTribe of Priestswith close ties to the Royal Family andMagitekwith predominantly blueTron Lines, have some connection to Nayru, but the connection isn't nearly as explicit as with the Zora.

characters.name: Farore
characters.description: Goddess of Courage, represented by the forests, wind, lightning, the color green, and the Kokiri and Deku races. Once Nayru created the law of the land, Farore created life itself, all creatures and plant life, to uphold that law. Creating Life: She created all life in Hyrule. Dragons Are Divine: According to lore in the Era of the Wild games, dragons are symbolically associated with Farore and courage. Ethnic Goddess: She is associated with the Kokiri, a plantlike race with close connections to nature associated with the color green. The fact that the Hero of Time incarnation of Link, the first to wield Farore's Triforce of Courage, was raised among them is also significant. By extension, the Koroks are also associated with Farore. Fertility Goddess: Farore was the goddess who created life. Though she is mostly known as the Goddess of Courage, and is specifically the one who blesses and empowers the chosen hero, her other blessings and sacred relics may also help various forms of life flourish.

characters.name: The Triforce
characters.description: Also known as the Golden Power, Power of the Gods, and the Prime Energy, these three triangular artifacts were left behind when the Golden Goddesses returned to the heavens after creating Hyrule. It consists of the Triforce of Power (the top piece), the Triforce of Wisdom (the bottom left piece), and the Triforce of Courage (the bottom right piece). Any mortal who holds all three pieces will be granted the ability to achieve whatever one desires, and even holding just one piece will give its wielder unmatched magic power. Many wars were fought for possession of the Triforce, requiring those sworn to protect Hyrule to seal it away and suppress knowledge of it. Link, Zelda, and Ganon are the only people shown to consistently keep hold of pieces of the Triforce. Several games portray the Triforce as a sapient entity on its own. Apple of Discord: The mere rumor of its existence has a history of causingGreat Offscreen Warsthroughout the series, since its omnipotent power is justtoo temptingfor corrupt individuals to ignore. Its very existence has to be closely guarded by the Royal Family of Hyrule for this reason. Benevolent Genie: Yes and no. The Triforce cannot and will not distinguish between a good wish and an evil wish — however, it can speak to its owners and offer guidance, and its very being contains several failsafes to prevent an evil owner from attaining absolute power. If touched by someone without a proper balance of seeking Power, Wisdom and Courage, it will only grant him or her the piece they most embody and then hide inside those who embody the other two. If this doesn't work and the Triforce is re-combined, then the power and application of the wish still depends on the heart and will, as well as whether or not they possess those three virtues. If you still lack Courage and Wisdom, then you will make a cowardly, stupid wish and the Triforce will give youexactly what you asked for. characters.name: Hylia
characters.description: Hyrule's original protector goddess. She is the original identity of the very first Zelda, until she took a human form and began her plans to defeat evil. Her statues are magically-imbued sites of great importance for Link's quests inSkyward SwordandBreath of the Wild. She continuously reincarnates alongside Link as her descendants, Zelda. Action Girl: She forged the Goddess Sword and originally wielded it against the Demon King Demise, before passing it down to her chosen Hero. Adaptation Expansion: She appears in a prequel manga included inHyrule Historia, wherein she chooses the first incarnation of Link as her champion against Demise, and forsakes her immortality after he is killed to be reincarnated at his side. Big Good: While she is subordinate to the Golden Goddesses, Hylia is the deity who protected Hyrule and the Triforce in the series' backstory. She is the one that started the Royal Family, defeated Demise, created the first iteration of the Master Sword, and chose the first Hero. Celestial Paragons and Archangels: Statues depict her as a winged woman wielding the Goddess Sword.

characters.name: The Master Sword
characters.description: The legendary Blade of Evil's Bane often wielded by the Hero of Hyrule. It is later revealed to house a mind of its own named Fi. Ambiguously Sentient Object: The Master Sword has been described throughout the series from as early asOcarina of Timeas having a mind of its own, but whether this was literal, indirect (due to it beingForged by the Gods), or merely metaphorical wasn't explored untilSkyward Sword— canonically the firstZeldagame in the series' timeline — which reveals it to have a personification in the form of a spirit named Fi. At the end of the game,Fi would become permanently dormant within the Master Sword, retroactively placing her in the series' mythos, but leaving it uncertain if this meant that Fi actually still "exists" in the games as we know her.Breath of the WildandTears of the Kingdomallude to this with brief scenes of Zelda and Linkwordlessly "hearing" somethingfrom the Master Sword that goes unspoken to the audience — whether this is Fi herself communicating or something else about the sword is also left unconfirmed. Barrier Maiden: Was originally used as the final key to the Sacred Realm to prevent anyone unworthy from claiming the Triforce. By the time ofThe Wind Waker, most of her power was sacrificed in order to both seal Hyrule Castle and diminish Ganondorf's power. The Hero of the Winds manages to recharge the sword to defeat Ganondorf once again. Bookends:In games such asA Link to the Past,Ocarina of Time, andTwilight Princess, the Master Sword is first seen when Link pulls it from a pedestal. When peace is achieved, he returns the sword.InThe Wind Waker, Link pulls the Master Sword from a pedestal in the submerged Hyrule Castle. At the end, Link buries the Master Sword into Ganondorf's head, turning him into a new stone pedestal and ensuring that neither will ever reach the surface again.InTears of the Kingdom, the Sword is retrieved by pulling it from the head of the Light Dragon, aka, a draconified Zelda. characters.name: Great Deku Tree
characters.description: A huge tree and the fatherly guardian of the forest, the Koroks, and guardian of Farore's Pearl. The Artifact: Likely due to his extreme age, his moniker is the only instance of the term "Deku" still being used on the Great Sea. Otherwise, it's been replaced with "Boko" to refer to forest-related objects and enemies. Continuity Nod: He feels a rush of nostalgia at the sight of the Hero's Clothes that Link is wearing. Of course he would; in-universe, the clothes are modeled after the green garb of the Hero of Time—the Kokiri Tunic. Does This Remind You of Anything?: The Chu-Chus popping up over his face looks like a bad case of an acne breakout. Divine Delegation: He has a grand vision for new forests to be planted so that the land lost during the Great Flood will eventually be reclaimed from the depths. Since he's immobile, he tasks his Koroks with this mission.

characters.name: Lord Jabu-Jabu
characters.description: A giant fish worshipped as a guardian spirit for the Zora. He is best known for hisinnards serving as dungeons in themselves. Cool Crown: He wears a crown to signify his status as a god of the Zora. Electric Jellyfish: Both times his body serves as a dungeon, he is beset by a parasite in the form of a Biri/BariKing Mook: Barinade inOcarina of Timeand Plasmarine inOracle of Ages. Even inEchoes of Wisdom, where his body isn't a dungeon, another form of Barinade can be fought as anOptional Bossfor aSide Questnot too far away. Ethnic God: Whenever he appears, he is considered the patron deity of the Zora. Gentle Giant: Despite being enormous, he is said to be very kind and loving to the Zora who worship him and even Hylians who pay him homage.

characters.name: Impa
characters.description: Impa is a name given to each Zelda's attendant/nursemaid, though many characters of the name are quite different from one another. In most of her incarnations, she is a member of the mysterious Sheikah tribe and generally the leader of the tribe (if notthe last of her kind). Beyond that, she tends to be either a youthful warrior who serves as Zelda's bodyguard or an elderly sage who provides Link with guidance and advice. Action Girl: In some incarnations, she seems less a nanny and closer to a bodyguard. In general, Impa is either a young Sheikah not unlike a ninja, or she's an old and possibly portly woman. InSkyward Sword, she's both. Even the elderly version from the NES games managed to escape capture and survive monster attacks long enough to find Link. Likewise, inEchoes of Wisdom, despite being an elderly woman, she's shown to be capable of beating up multiple castle guards at once. All There in the Manual: She never made an on-screen appearance untilWand of Gamelon/Ocarina of Time.In the NES games, she only showed up in the manuals. Cool Old Lady: When she isn't a youngNinja, she comes across as this. Dark Is Not Evil: InOcarina of TimeandSkyward Sword, she's a fearsome-lookingNinjawho dresses in predominantly dark colors and in the former game is specifically the "Sage of Shadow" whose associated temple is anundead crypt. She's nonetheless a good and heroic character utterly devoted to Zelda's safety.

characters.name: Kings of Hyrule
characters.description: The rulers of Hyrule whenever Princess Zelda isn'truling on her own. Most Kings mentioned in the stories have been Zelda's father, though there have also been games that portrayed Kings who were her distant ancestors instead. The Ghost: Early on, the king was usually referred to but never seen. This is most prominent inOcarina of Time, where Link can peer through a window at Ganondorf bowing before the king but can't see the king himself. The Good King: They've generally been portrayed as kind and just rulers. Even King Rhoam appears to be a decent ruler who cares about his daughter despite hisFantasy-Forbidding Fathertendencies. The High King: Usually, the king theoretically rule over all the races of Hyrule, but the lesser kings, chieftains and village elders mostly run local things on their own. Huge Guy, Tiny Girl: The Kings always tower over Zelda. King Rhoam in particular looks like he could easily lift her in one hand.

characters.name: Kaepora Gaebora
characters.description: The wise old owl who shows up inOcarina of Time,Majora's Mask, andFour Swords Adventures. A similar owl also appears inLink's Awakening, but is not named. He appears to give the player hints as to where to go next and what to do. Abnormal Limb Rotation Range: Frequently turns his head upside-down. Exposition Fairy: His main purpose is to give the player information. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Even though he is described as an owl, he has a number of elements that draw from the great hormed owl, one of the largest living species of owls, most notably with the "eyebrows", the call heard inFour Swords Adventures, and his overall size, which has more in line with eagles. Giant Flyer: InOcarina of Time, he's able to pick Link up and fly him from Lake Hylia to Hyrule Castle.

characters.name: Rauru
characters.description: The Sage of Light and a leading member of the Sages, Rauru made his debut inOcarina of Time. Ambiguous Situation:Although it has been confirmed that he is the true identity of the Kaepora Gaebora shown inOcarina of Time, there is no indication there is a Terminan counterpart of him inMajora's Mask.Breath of the Wildhas a location called Rauru Hillside, although it is not clear if it's named after the original Rauru or his Zonai incarnation. Although it has been confirmed that he is the true identity of the Kaepora Gaebora shown inOcarina of Time, there is no indication there is a Terminan counterpart of him inMajora's Mask. Breath of the Wildhas a location called Rauru Hillside, although it is not clear if it's named after the original Rauru or his Zonai incarnation. Animal Motifs: Rauru is associated with owls, reflecting his wisdom.InOcarina of Time, he can take on the form of Kaepora Gaebora to communicate with the outside world.InTears of the Kingdom, he wears an owl pendant.

characters.name: The Sages
characters.description: A group of people with special powers that they use to support Link and Zelda - usually afterLink has to rescue them. The title of Sage is a hereditary one (though not by blood) and the identities of the Sages change with each game they're in, though Zelda is usually considered one and if Impa is in a game with Sages in it, then she's one too. Barrier Maiden: They always have some major role to play in keeping Hyrule safe, whether that be sealing Ganon away, maintaining that seal, or granting Link the ability to use or continue using divine artifacts against the villains. Chekhov's Gunman: InOcarina of TimeandA Link Between Worlds, you meet each of the Sages (except for Rauru) in the early parts of the game long before you (or eventhey) realize theyarea Sage. The Chosen One: Various games in the series show that the candidates to become Sages are born with their roles rather than choosing them. They remain unknowing of their power until the time in which they're needed. At which point, they'll feel a strange, instinctive compulsion to go to their associated temples. Once they do, and it's purged of any evil influence, they awaken their powers and immediately understand how to do their duties. Damsel in Distress: Ganon and other bad guys usually target the Sages and imprison them at the beginning of the game, forcing Link to rescue them. Some of them areDistressed Dudesinstead, but "damsel" is more common (A Link to the PastandFour Swords Adventuresspecifically make them the SevenMaidens).

characters.name: Malon
characters.description: The girl from Lon Lon Ranch inOcarina of Time, who also appears as a minor NPC in other games, fromOracle of SeasonstoThe Minish Cap. She's the one who gives Link his horse, Epona. Ocarina'sMalon herself is the second version of the character, the first having a starring role as "Marin" from Link's Awakening. Aryll fromThe Wind Wakeris meant to be another incarnation of the archetype and was named "Maryll" early in development. Ilia inTwilight Princessis another counterpart, albeit as a semi-prominent character in that game. Kina fromSkyward Swordis yet another close counterpart, and in an even lesser role, Falfa fromEchoes of Wisdomserves her role at Hyrule Ranch. Betty and Veronica: In games where they both appear and have some amount ofShip Teasewith Link, Malon or her expies will typically be the Betty to another character, due to being the more humble, modestly-dressed and simple girl compared to Princess Zelda, or whomever else is prominent in the game like Ilia to Midna. Even from afar, this can be seen with Link falling for the simple island girl Marin despite (or maybe even because of) her resemblance to Hyrule's princess. Demoted to Extra:Has happened to Malon specifically over the course of her legacy. InLink's Awakening, Marin is a major character, having saved Link upon arriving on Koholint Island and teaching him the Ballad of the Wind Fish. InOcarina of Time, while not a major character, Malon proves vital in helping Link get into Hyrule Castle and later is the one who gives him Epona. In all games since, she's a very minor character, only providing minor sidequests at best.Her archetype zig-zags. She can be as crucial to the plot as Ilia is toTwilight Princess, or only relevant to sidequests like Kina inSkyward Swordand Falfa inEchoes of Wisdom. Has happened to Malon specifically over the course of her legacy.
