characters.name: Talon
characters.description: The owner of Lon Lon Ranch and Malon's father. He's good-natured but somewhat lazy. He shows up in every game that Malon does. Bumbling Dad: Malon is much more level headed than he is, and better liked. Heavy Sleeper: AFetch QuestinOcarina of TimeandOracle of Seasonsinvolves finding an item to wake him up. Lazy Bum: He has a bad tendency to fall asleep in out-of-the-way places and typically spends hours at a time asleep. Quests featuring him typically involve the need to wake him up. Race Lift: InOracle of SeasonsandFour Swords Adventures, he seems to be a regular human, whereas he is usually a Hylian.

characters.name: Ingo
characters.description: The Luigi to Talon's Mario, sometimes called Gorman. Unlike Talon, he tends to be grouchy and overbearing. Decomposite Character: InOcarina of Timeand most subsequent games, Ingo is a single character. InMajora's Mask, he has three Terminian counterparts, the Gorman brothers, who look like him. Early-Installment Weirdness: His earliest incarnation inLink's Awakeningwas an unnamed Cucco Keeper who was completely disconnected from the story, not even relevant to any sidequests. Jerkass Has a Point: While making Malon his servant under threat of abusing the horses was cruel, he wasn't wrong that Talon was aLazy BuminOcarina of Time. Talon agrees and promises to work harder once returning to the ranch. Leaning on the Fourth Wall: InOracle of Seasons, Ingo is a collector of pottery who complains about how people seem to always have the urge to break them.

characters.name: Anju
characters.description: A stressed woman who needs Link's help with a sidequest, usually something involving Cuccos. Ascended Extra: Has by far the longest and most elaborate sidequest inMajora's Mask. Early-Installment Weirdness: Was unnamed inOcarina of Time. Hysterical Woman: Almost always panicking or moping. Irony: Is a Cucco Keeper inOcarina of TimeandThe Minish Capwho is terrible at catching escaped Cuccos.

characters.name: Baito
characters.description: A laid-back man who holds a part-time job. A Dog Named "Perro": Baito is Japanese slang for a part-timer. Everyone Calls Him "Barkeep": InMajora's Maskand the Japanese version ofWind Waker, he is only referred to as the Part-Timer. Named by the Dub: The English version ofWind Wakerkept the word "Baito" as his actual name rather than translating it as "Part Timer" like inMajora's Mask. Sitting on the Roof: His defining characteristic inOcarina of Time. He gives you a Piece of Heart if you manage to climb up to his spot.

characters.name: Mutoh and Carpenters
characters.description: An irritable foreman and his crew. Early-Installment Weirdness: Mutoh was unnamed inOcarina of Time. Inconsistent Spelling: While Mutoh's name is unchanged inPhantom Hourglass, his knights have fancier versions of the names they had inThe Minish Cap(Doyle is now Doylan, for example). Later-Installment Weirdness: Their incarnations inPhantom Hourglassare not carpenters but rather a king and hisElite Fourknights. Mean Boss: Mutoh berates and criticizes his men all the time, but is willing to praise them when they succeed.

characters.name: Biggoron
characters.description: A Goron who is very big. Usually involved in a sidequest that gets you a powerful item. Artifact Name: Downplayed inPhantom Hourglass; he's still the biggest Goron, but nowhere near the kaiju size he was in previous games. Blessed with Suck: InOracle of Seasons, his large size means he can't take shelter from the heavy Winter caused by Onox's screwing with the weather. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: His brother Medigoron stopped appearing after the N64 games. Giant's Knife; Human's Greatsword: Medigoron'sGiant's Knifeand his own Biggoron Sword are too heavy for Link to carry in one hand (except inSoul Calibur 2where doing so causes Link to lose health with each swing).

characters.name: Happy Mask Salesman
characters.description: A cheery (usually) and enigmatic man who runs a mask business. Ascended Extra: His masks were mostly novelties inOcarina of Time, but inMajora's Maskhelping him out is the main goal. Eyes Always Shut: Except when he'snothappy. Identical Stranger: The Moon Children fromMajora's Masklook identical to him with their masks off. Mood-Swinger:After the first rewind inMajora's Mask, he starts happy when teaching Link the Song of Healing, gets furious when he finds Link didn't get the Mask back, alternates between sobbing and ranting about the Mask's dangers, turns to pathetically pleading for Link to help him, and is all smiles again when Link agrees to do so.InOracle of Ageshe cycles between somberly moaning about his hunger and furiously screaming about it.

characters.name: Guru-Guru
characters.description: A jolly (usually) man who is perpetually playing the Song of Storms on his phonograph and is usually the caretaker of a windmill. Ambiguously Related: To the Happy Mask Salesman, both being usually smiling men who gain aNightmare Facewhen enraged. In fact, the texture for his angry eyes is the same as the Salesman's, just with the pupils removed, and his mouth texture when angry is the Salesman's smile turned upside down. The Artifact: He still plays the Song of Storms inMajora's MaskandOracle of Seasons, but Link does not learn it from him and his sidequests in those games have nothing to do with storms. Early-Installment Weirdness: Like many other characters, he was unnamed inOcarina of Time. Eyes Always Shut: Much like the Happy Mask Salesman, he only opens his whennothappy.

characters.name: Tingle
characters.description: The goofy-looking man who rides around by tying a balloon to his belt, floating in the air drawing maps. He first meets Link inMajora's Maskwhere he's jealous that Link has aFairy Companionbecause he thinks that he's the very reincarnation of a fairy. He later appears inThe Wind Waker,where he charges 398 Rupees apiece to translate the Triforce Charts. Adaptational Badass: Certain games make him out to be deceptively tough, particularly those that place him in the protagonist role. Adaptational Villainy: InFour Swords Adventureshis primary role is to swoop in when a large amount of force gems are on screen and try to steal them from the Links. It's his only appearance where he's an outrightdetrimentto the player. Americans Hate Tingle: Although loved and cherished in Japan and some parts of Europe, he isdespisedin America and several other countries, to the point he's theTrope Namerfor the trope of "a character is received in starkly different manners in different countries".invoked Breakout Character: Stars in threeSpin-Offgames:Freshly-Picked Tingle's Rosy Rupeeland, a Tingle-themed reskin ofBalloon Fight, and aDating Sim/The Wizard of Oz (1939)parody calledRipened Tingle's Balloon Trip of Love. All were exclusive to Japan except forTingle's Rosy Rupeeland, which was released in Europe.

characters.name: Postman
characters.description: Early-Installment Weirdness: His first two incarnations inA Link to the PastandOcarina of Timewere not postmen but generic "running men", though the latter's descendants were postmen according toWind Waker. The former also bore little resemblance to the later incarnations. Inexplicably Awesome: TheTwilight PrincessPostman can not only recognize Link when he's in Wolf form, he can make it all the way to the final floor of the Cave of Ordeals. Offscreen Teleportation: You cannot win the "race" against him inOcarina of Time, he's always waiting for you at the entrance to Kokiri Forest, claiming he beat you by a second. InTwilight Princess,Phantom Hourglass, andSpirit Tracks, he shows up to give you a letter the moment you fulfill the requirements to receive one. Schedule Fanatic: TheMajora's MaskPostman is always either on his mail route or at home training for his mail route, unless Link gets him relieved from duty on the final day. Silly Walk: TheSpirit TracksPostman imitates a train chugging along as he runs.

characters.name: Epona
characters.description: Link's trusty steed. Link either has to obtain Epona from a ranch or starts with Epona from the beginning of the game, although in that case, it's guaranteed that Epona will soon run off, and Link has to find her again. Ascended Extra: As commonly as Epona appeared in promotional materials forOcarina of Time, you can technically beat the game without obtaining her as a mount or even visiting Lon Lon Ranch. But youdoneed her to jump over otherwise impassable fences inMajora's Mask, and she's not only needed for similar navigation inTwilight Princessbut also for mounted combat, to the point that you need to ride her for one phase of theFinal Boss. Automaton Horse: She never requires any sort of care, other than theSprint Meterthat prevents unlimited spurring to full gallop. Averted inBreath of the Wild, along with all the other horses. Badass Adorable: InMajora's Mask,where she's still a filly, carries Link into battle, and manages to make her way to Romani Ranch on her own after escaping the Skull Kid. The Cameo: Appears as a carthorse inMinish Cap, pulling the Lon Lon Ranch goods to market. If you speak to her while Minish-sized, she'll ask you to buy some milk to lighten her load.

characters.name: Beedle
characters.description: A local sea merchant of the Great Sea, traveling from island to island with practical goods at hand. He hasn't gotten much luck in his business venture until Link sets foot in his doorstep. Ambiguously Brown: At a time when the only dark-skinned humanoids in the Zelda games were theGerudo, he was the first and occasionally only non-Gerudo to be portrayed with dark skin. Beetle Maniac: He has a beetle symbol on his shorts, and his name is a pun on Beetle. According to his figurine, he is fond of bugs, especially beetles. Boring, but Practical: Beedle doesn't offer anything rare or fancy (unless he's Masked Beedle), but his exclusive goods are essential for Link's quest. The All-Purpose Bait can lure Fishmen, pigs and rats into the vicinity, the Hyoi Pear allows Link to control a seagull, and both must be placed in their own Bait Bag also sold by Beedle. Catchphrase: "OHHHH!" whenever he sees a customer entering his shop.

characters.name: Old Man
characters.description: A nameless old man who gives advice to Link. He first meets Link inthe first gameand has made sporadic appearances since. Despite a prominent role as a giver of items and advice, the Old Man is never given a name, and has little identity in the story. Often there are actually several unnamed old men. Up untilBreath of the Wild, the Old Man only appeared in the 2DZeldagames. Other wise old men directly inspired by this archetype, like Sahasrahla, have appeared in other games, but are set apart by greater individual characterization. Betting Mini-Game: In one location, an Old Man in the first game makes Link pick three rupees which either make Link gain or lose money."Let's play money making game." Composite Character: The Old Man inBreath of the Wildfulfills the typical role of the character and is also the King of Hyrule.

characters.name: Syrup & Maple
characters.description: An old witch who sells Link potions and magic powder, and her granddaughter, who works as her shopkeeper and rides a flying broom, although rather badly. The Bus Came Back: The fact that the Lorulean counterpart to the witch fromA Link Between Worldsis referred to as "Mapes" implies that she's supposed to be a grown up Maple, who hadn't otherwise been seen since 2002 (2001 if you discount theLink to the Pastremake). Cute Witch: In theOraclegames, Maple is a cute-looking young girl who flies around (awkwardly) on a broomstick. Irene, her implied granddaughter inA Link Between Worlds, inherited the cute look. Flying Broomstick: Maple flies around on a broomstick, although she's rather bad at it and prone to crashing. If she makes enough money in the Oracle games, she eventually trades it out for a flying vacuum cleaner. Generation Xerox: It's implied that the witch fromA Link Between Worldsis actually Maple from theA Link to the PastGBA port, having taken on the same role and overall appearance as her grandmother Syrup. Likewise, her own granddaughter Irene is the spitting image of Maple in her own youth.

characters.name: Hands in Toilets
characters.description: Bizarre, apparently undead hands residing in toilets who crave paper. Helping Hands: They're apparently undead hands who can talk and demand paper. While it's ambiguous whether the hands inMajora's MaskandOracle of Ageshave an attached body, Phoeni, the hand inSkyward Swordis explicitly only a hand in her ghostly state. No Name Given: The hands are normally unnamed, usually going by "???" if referred to in-game. However, the Prima guide forSkyward Swordgave its hand a name, "Phoeni", which was adopted by the HD remaster for the Switch. Running Gag: TheZeldaseries is no stranger to recurring jokes, but this one stands out as one of the weirdest of them all. Toilet Humor: A surrealRunning Gagabout hands that treat writing paper as toilet paper.

characters.name: Dampé
characters.description: An old man with an intimidating appearance, usually acting as a gravekeeper. Crusty Caretaker: He is a gravekeeper with a distinctly ugly face and tends to live secluded from others to stay near his graveyard. Face of a Thug: Despite looking scary to the point of having to live separate from others, he's always friendly and helpful towards Link. Gonk: He has a very odd appearance, having a bald head, hunched back, an asymmetrical face, and stuck-out teeth. The Hermit: Dampé lives in secluded areas, partly because most people are intimidated by him. He's still kind and gracious to visitors in spite of this, however.

characters.name: Dark Link
characters.description: Link'sDoppelgängerwho first appears as "Link's Shadow" inZelda II: The Adventure of Link, as the surprise final boss. He's something of a popular character with the fandom despite his infrequent appearances and lack of characterization. He appears most notably inOcarina of Timeas the mini-boss in theWater Temple, and inFour Swords AdventuresandEchoes of Wisdomas aRecurring Boss. There are many different Dark Links, just as there are many different Links. The character is alternately known as Link's Shadow (inThe Adventure of Link), Dark Link (inOcarina of TimeandEchoes of Wisdom), and Shadow Link (inFour Swords Adventures); it is unknown if there are any meaningful differences between these names. InThe Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds, you can enter Shadow Link Battles as aStreetPassfeature. They represent other players you pass and are equipped with up to two of the items they have. Big, Bulky Bomb: Shadow Link throws humongous bombs at you several times duringFour Swords Adventures. Can also use them inA Link Between Worldsshould an opposing player equip them with one. The Blank: In many of his appearances, he has no facial features except for glowing red eyes, and sometimes not even that. Degraded Boss: InOracle of Ages, Veran can create Dark Link doppelgangers as easily defeatedMooks.

characters.name: Phantom Ganon
characters.description: An evil wraith that has been summoned by Ganondorf several times, sharing several of his master's powers and acting in his stead. Artifact Name: He's called Phantom Ganon inOcarina of Timedue to looking exactly like his master except for hisSkull for a Head. This name is less fitting for theLiving Shadowdepictions fromThe Wind WakerandFour Swords Adventures, who only vaguely resemble the Demon King, to the point that first-time players might not even know that they're up against Phantom Ganon. On the other hand,Tears of the Kingdomdepicts him as a Gloom copy of Ganondorf's mummified body. BFS: InThe Wind WakerandFour Swords Adventures, he carries a large black falchion with a curl at the tip. The Bus Came Back:Tears of the Kingdommarks his first mainline game appearance sinceFour Swords Adventures19 years earlier. Dark Is Evil: He started off as an undead-looking monster at first, and then seemed to transition into aLiving Shadow.

characters.name: Twinrova
characters.description: The twin sisters Koume and Kotake, who were Ganon's adoptive parents inOcarina of Time, are the true villains of theOraclegames. They send Onox and Veran to Holodrum and Labrynna to create destruction and sorrow as part of a plan to resurrect the Demon King, Ganon. Big Bad Duumvirate: They are behind bothOraclegames as the bosses of Onox and Veran, and they are one entity in two forms. Color-Coded Elements: In their fused form, Twinrova will randomly switch between using the elements offire(red) andice(blue), with her appearance changing accordingly. (These colors correspond, respectively, to Koume and Kotake, who are predominantly colored as such.) Interestingly, when they first merge together or when damaged enough by Link to be stunned, Twinrova is an even split of both; her left half is icy and her right is fire. Crystal Ball: They use one to spy on Link. Dark Action Girl: Koume and Kotake are wicked old crones who are respectively mistresses of fire and ice magic and can literally combine their powers into one youthful, more powerful Gerudo witch.

characters.name: Vaati
characters.description: A mysterious robed figure who wins the Picori Festival's swordfighting tournament. His goal is to obtain the Light Force and become a god. Ambiguous Start of Darkness: Although Ezlo explains that Vaati became interested in humanity's potential for evil and tried to follow their example, he cannot say for sure whether he became that way over time or was always aDeceptive Disciple. The manga adaptation depicts Vaati breaking down from serving as Ezlo'sBeleaguered Assistant. Badass Bookworm: He gained all of his knowledge about the legendary Picori Blade and Princess Zelda's Light Force from reading. In addition, he studied sorcery (though a lot of help came from that hat perched atop his head) and the psychology of evil inside of the hearts of men. He is averyphysical villain, too — when there is something to be done, he often does it himself. Badass Cape: Look at his cover photo! The Bad Guy Wins:If you take too long tostop his ritualat the end of the game, he will drain Zelda of all the Light Force, leaving her dead, and him very much an invincible god you can't defeat,spelling instant game over.

characters.name: Arrghus
characters.description: A cyclopean creature that protects itself with a cloud of smaller minions. Dub Name Change: From "Wart" in Japanese. Strangely, itsMajora's Maskappearance keeps the name "Wart" in English versions, although other language dubs use the same name for it as for other games' versions of the boss. Eye Beams: Some incarnations of Arrghus can fire lasers from their central eyes. Flunky Boss: It protects itself with small jellyfish called Arrgi or just flying eyeballs, and uses them to attack Link as well; the Stone Arrghus inFour Swords Adventuresuses rocks for the same purpose. TheFour Swordsadd-on forA Link to the Pastalso has Baris. Oculothorax: It resembles either a jellyfish-like creature with a single huge eye dominating its body or just a giant floating eyeball.

characters.name: Gleeok
characters.description: A dragon with many heads, which remain animated after being cut and continue to fly around and breathe fire at Link until the whole monster is killed. A two-headed Gleeok is the boss of Level Four, a three-headed one is a miniboss in Level Six, and a four-headed one is the boss of Level Eight. Adapted Out: Does not appear in the Satellaview remake. Breath Weapon: It spits fireballs. Degraded Boss: Inverted. Like Gohma, the mid-boss versions you encounter later on have more heads and are therefore more dangerous than the one you face at the end of Level 4. Multiple Head Case: Depending on the specific one fought, Gleeok can have anywhere from two to four heads.

characters.name: Gohma
characters.description: Arthropod monsters with a giant vulnerable eye, Gohmas are some of the most common recurring bosses in the franchise. Gohma first appeared in the original game, and additionally features inLink's Awakening,Ocarina of Time,Oracle of Seasons,Four Swords AdventuresandThe Wind Waker. The similarly-named and -fought Armogohma and Marbled Gohma appear inTwilight PrincessandTears of the Kingdomrespectively. All Webbed Up: The Gohma inEchoes of Wisdomcan spit spider webs in battle and also what made the Deku Scrubs of Faron Wetlands hooked on their cotton candy. Cyclops: They only have a single, massive eye — which, naturally, is their only weak spot. Eye Beams: Some versions can shoot beams or fireballs from their eyes. Giant Enemy Crab: Varies between this andGiant Spider. They are usually depicted as gigantic cyclopean crabs in the 2D titles, although the Gohmas inOcarina of TimeandThe Wind Wakeralso resembles nonspecific monstrous crustaceans.

characters.name: Manhandla
characters.description: A ferocious plant with snapping maws, Mandhandla moves faster as each head is severed. It serves as the boss of Level Three, and is also found in Level Four and Level Eight. Beef Gate: The Manhandla that is the boss of Level Three is incredibly hard to kill with any weapon weaker than the White Sword; it has four different heads to kill, each one takes four strikes with the Wooden Sword to destroy, and it gets progressively faster and harder to dodge as it loses its heads. It's very difficult to pass it before getting the White Sword (or before learning about Manhandla's bomb weakness). Breath Weapon: It spits fireballs. Clean Dub Name: Its name is changed from Testitart to Manhandla for the English version, probably because the Japanese name sounded too close to testicles. Crossover Cameo: According to the Japanese instruction booklet, it's aKing Mookfor the Piranha Plant fromSuper Mario Bros.. This is removed from localized manuals.

characters.name: Volvagia
characters.description: A serpentine, fire-breathing dragon. It is typically fought in arenas filled with large holes, where the dragon pops in and out of shelther while attacking. Breath Weapon: Like any good dragon, he breathes fire for his main form of attack. The Bus Came Back: Volvagia returns in his original form inEchoes of Wisdomafter being absent sinceOcarina of Time(discountingalternate variants).Granted, it's actually a Tecuum of the real Volvagia. Dragons Are Demonic: Draconic enemies are a frequent fixture of a fantasy series likeZelda, but Volvagia is one of the most recurrent types to serve as a boss. Dub Name Change: His name was originally shortened to "Barba" from the original Japanese (バルバジア;Barubajia) for the original English localization ofZelda II.Ocarina of Timelater changed it to the more faithful "Volvagia", which has since stuck.

characters.name: Armos and Beamos
characters.description: Composite Character: The Decayed Guardians and Guardian Turrets fromBreath of the Wildare basically Armos (statue-like enemies that stay dormant until you get close to them) crossed with Beamos (one-eyed laser turret enemies), the latter of which reappear in the game itself, though they're only encountered in the Sheikah Shrines. They're generally much more powerful, though, and the regular kind are mobile from the start and less like Armos as a result. Distinction Without a Difference: The Guardians ofBreath of the Wildlargely play their role with their stone bodies andEye Beams, but their names make no reference to Armos and Beamos. Magitek: They've frequently had this design starting withThe Wind Waker, complete withTron Lines. Mecha-Mook: They are mechanical beings made to guard rooms and objects. ALiving Statuethat chases Link. They are usually found within dungeons or around their entrances, and are particularly common around ruins. Their abilities and appearance change greatly from game to game.

characters.name: Bari and Biri
characters.description: Electrified jellyfish-like enemies typically found in dungeons. The larger Bari tend to split into smaller Biri when killed. Asteroids Monster: Some Bari split into two or three Biri when defeated. Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: In the 2D games, a Bari's color determines whether it will split into Biri on defeat: red and yellow ones do so, while blue and green ones don't. Electric Jellyfish: Both Biri and Bari are highly electrified, requiring Link to wait for them to power down to attack them or to use ranged weapons against them. Flying Seafood Special: Jellyfish that float about in the air. This is averted inTwilight Princess, where they instead are found underwater in the Lakebed Temple.

characters.name: Blins
characters.description: Common goblin and orc-like monsters whose names all end in the suffix "-blin". Designs have ranged from imp-like to bulldog-like to boar-like (this motif seems to be the most popular). There are many subspecies of this race: The original subspecies is theMoblin, a spear-wielding savage that served as common foes in earlier installments. Later 3D installments have them as the strongest, most elite members of the Blins, but they remain as common foes in 2D games. They are often found in forest areas. TheBokoblins, introduced inWind Waker, are about the size of an average Hylian, but fight with relatively more finesse than their larger counterparts. They tend to be common foes in later 3D installments, and are the first enemies encountered inBreath of the Wild. Miniblins, also introduced inWind Waker, are the smallest and weakest of the Blin race, but attack in large groups to make up for this. Bulblins, introduced inTwilight Princess, are similar to Bokoblins, but can be skilled archers and ride boar-like Bullbos. Some of their traits were absorbed into the Bokoblins in later games.

characters.name: Bubbles
characters.description: Despite the name, these things are flaming disembodied skulls, often winged, that usually curse Link when he touches them. Artifact Name: The name "Bubbles" for this monster made a lot more sense when they just looked like blue or red circles. Now that they've been modeled to look more like demonic flaming skulls, the name seems absolutely bizarre. Dem Bones: They appear as a flying skull (sometimes with bat-like wings) that surrounds itself in a globe of ghostly flames. Evil Counterpart Race: Bubbles are identified as "Anti Fairies" at least in the localizations ofA Link to the Pastand the Game Boy games. In addition to to also being small flying balls of light, these games also allow the player to turn Bubbles into friendly fairies. Later games drop this distinction. An Ice Person:Twilight Princessonwards introduces the Ice Bubbles, which can freeze Link on contact.

characters.name: Buzz Blobs and Cukemen
characters.description: ABlob Monsterwhich shocks Link when attacked with the sword. Using certain items on it turns it into the mysterious Cukeman creature who spouts weird advice andFourth Wall Breakinglines. They continue to make sporadic appearances in later 2D games, but their role is mainly filled in the 3D games by electric variants of the Chuchu. Black Bead Eyes: Their eyes are small black dots when in Buzz Blob form. Blob Monster: An early one in the series, until the Chuchu largely replaced them and similar enemies. The Goomba: The Blobs, a variant introduced inA Link Between Worldsare normal Buzz Blobs that resemble their appearance prior to said game, but don't have their protective electricity.

characters.name: Chuchus
characters.description: A fairly weak blob creature available in a wide range of colors and types, with each color normally yielding a useful spoil. Weak blob creatures have featured in numerous earlyZeldagames (Bits and Bots, Zols, and Buzz Blobs), but the Chuchu has seemingly become a default replacement for all of them. Aquatic Mook: The Blue Chuchus inSkyward Swordcan only be found in underwater areas, though they can't electrocute Link. Asteroids Monster: An attribute stolen from the earlier Zols and Gels, large Chuchus split into smaller ones inTwilight PrincessandSkyward Sword. Blob Monster: A pretty weak one, too, though they can still be dangerous. Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: Chuchus always come in a number of different colors, which correspond to the sorts of items they drop on dying and/or to their offensive capabilities, making it easy to tell what you're in for as soon as you see one.

characters.name: Corrupted Soldiers
characters.description: Soldiers and guards of Hyrule who have been corrupted by evil. They attack in large numbers and can use a variety of weapons. Artifact Mook:To a degree in aA Link Between Worlds, where it's not explained why Yuga chose to create monsters based off the old uniform for the Hylian army.Averted in the Satellaview sequel toA Link to the Past, where all the guards are friendlyNPCsdue to it being post-World-Healing Wave. To a degree in aA Link Between Worlds, where it's not explained why Yuga chose to create monsters based off the old uniform for the Hylian army. Averted in the Satellaview sequel toA Link to the Past, where all the guards are friendlyNPCsdue to it being post-World-Healing Wave. Art Initiates Life: In most games, they're soldiers of Hyrule who have been corrupted. InA Link Between Worlds, they are paintings brought to life.

characters.name: Crows
characters.description: Large black birds that perch on trees and swoop down at Link when he passes by. In some games, Crows will also try to steal Link's Rupees when they attack.Basic Crows have a number of variants and related enemies, including theDacto, a pterosaur-like creature that behaves identically to them but is found in more remote area, and theTakkuri, a bizarre item-stealing bird fromMajora's Maskthat reappears inThe Minish Capas a recolor of the game's Crows. Airborne Mook: At their most basic, they're weak flying enemies that perch on trees and crags, taking flight when they spot Link and attacking him by swooping down at him from on high. Bandit Mook: InPhantom HourglassandSpirit Tracks, they will steal Link's Rupees when they hit him. They're also given this trait inEchoes of Wisdom, which can later beused to Zelda's advantagevia their echoes. Delicious Distraction: Crows can swarm over Echoes of Bait Zelda creates duringThe Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom, not unlike real life Vultures or other birds such as Pigeons gathering en masse to eat food left out for them. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart: Dactos, monstrous pterosaur-like creatures, replace Crows in the Dark World, Lorule and certain wasteland areas, but otherwise behave identically to them.

characters.name: Darknuts and Iron Knuckles
characters.description: Powerful knights with protective armor. The two, while having distinct names in English versions, are implied to be related in the Japanese scripts. Animated Armor: Some interpretations of Iron Knuckles suggest this, though at least one case explicitly shows that a person is inside the armor. Darknuts, however, are suggested to be living beings, and when Darknuts lose armor, they are shown to be creatures wearing armor. Artificial Brilliance: Darknuts have a history of being more clever than typicalZeldaenemies. InThe Wind Waker, they try to grab new weapons, such as a Moblin Spear, if Link disarms them, and will engage in hand-to-hand combat if they can't. They also tend to counter Link's Hurricane Spin with one of their own if they seem him charging it up. InTwilight Princess, a Darknut with its armor removed will hang back behind its fully armored companions, darting in and out to attack. Attack Its Weak Point: Normally, the only way to damage them is to hit a vulnerable gap in the armor. Beast Man: Darknuts inWind Wakerare depicted as jackal-like creatures underneath their armor.

characters.name: Deku Babas
characters.description: Man-eating Venus flytrap-like plants. Comes in several different variations. Attack Its Weak Point: Cutting its stem is aOne-Hit Kill. Bio Deku Babas and Baba Serpents keep moving when severed, though. InSkyward Sword, they can also be slashed across the mouth (though parrying its attacks will expose its stem for the old-fashioned way). Crossover Cameo: Deku Babas appear as stage hazards in aZelda-themed DLC course inMario Kart 8, replacing the usual Piranha Plants. Elite Mook: Several stronger variants on the usual Deku Baba have appeared in the games.Twilight Princesshas Baba Serpents, which can survive having their stem severed and will chase after Link when cut in this manner.Skyward Swordhas Quadro Babas, which have more health than the regular kind and can dodge Link's attacks. Twilight Princesshas Baba Serpents, which can survive having their stem severed and will chase after Link when cut in this manner.

characters.name: Dodongos
characters.description: Fire-breathing dinosaur dragons that are typically found close to lava. The most well-known method of killing them is throwing bombs down their throats. Armless Biped: InOcarina of TimeandMajora's Mask, Dodongos have only one set of legs that they drag themselves around with. Attack the Tail: Other than feeding it bombs, the tail is another recurring weak spot. Breath Weapon: InOcarina of Time,Majora's Mask,The Legend of Zelda: Four Swords Adventures, andTwilight Princess, they breathe fire. Defeat Equals Explosion: In some games, Dodongos violently explode upon dying.

characters.name: Eyegores
characters.description: Cyclopean statues or statue-like beings that animate and attack when Link approaches them. Achilles' Heel: Besides their single weak point in their eye, they can often only be harmed by arrows. Color-Coded for Your Convenience:A Link to the PastandA Link Between Worldssplit them between green, red and (in the latter) blue variants, the difference being that green Eyegores can be harmed by any weapon and red ones only by arrows. The second game drops this gimmick and makes the difference mostly cosmetic. Cyclops: They have a single giant eye dominating their faces, often to the exclusion of all other features. This is typically central to how they fight — they often become invulnerable when their eye is closed, may only be vulnerable there at all, and may shootEye Beamsfrom it. Eye Beams: InMajora's Mask, they attack Link by shooting beams from their eyes.

characters.name: Freezards
characters.description: Animated masses of ice that attempt to freeze Link solid with their icy breath, Freezards are almost always found inside ice dungeons. Asteroids Monster: InTwilight Princess, if killed with the Ball-and-Chain, a Freezard will shatter into a small group of Mini Freezards. Breath Weapon: They exhale icy wind that will freeze Link if it touches him. Extra Eyes: Freezards inTwilight Princesspossess a large number of eyes scattered across their fronts. Notably, when broken into Mini Freezards, each of the miniature shards will retain just one of their parent's eyes. An Ice Person: Living chunks of ice with freezing breath and a weakness to fire.

characters.name: Ghinis and Poes
characters.description: Ghostly beings that usually can't be attacked by normal means, often requiring an item to make them vulnerable. The difference between the two is that Poes carry lanterns, and that Ghinis only have one eye. They usually haunt cemeteries; Ghinis are only found there, but Poes are sometimes encountered in forests and other places. Generally, Ghinis are the older variant and have been around since the first game, while Poes debuted inA Link to the Past. Since then, Ghinis have been strictly found in handheld games, while Poes have appeared in both these and the 3D console titles. Bedsheet Ghost: Ghinis are one-eyed versions of this in early games — later titles tend to depict them as spherical, non-sheet specters instead. Cyclops: Ghinis have a single gigantic eye in the middle of their foreheads. Demoted to Extra: Poes appear inTears of the Kingdom, but strangely not as enemies. Rather they are merely collectibles that serve as the Depths' version of Rupees.

characters.name: Gibdos andReDeads
characters.description: Reanimated corpse-like monsters (mummies in the former case, zombies in the latter), with the former being in more games than the latter. While they're slow enemies, they can briefly paralyze Link, giving them an opportunity to rob him of several hearts. Airborne Mooks:Tears of the Kingdomintroduces the Moth Gibdos, an aerial version of the game's Gibdos. Ambiguously Human: Whether or notReDeadsare reanimated human corpses or artificial constructs of magic is unclear. While they most often look very organic, someSuper Smash Bros.trophies say they're made of clay, and inTri Force Heroes, this seems to be the case, as they are earth brown and can melt into puddles. BFS: InTwilight Princess, Gibdos, akaReDeadKnights, freeze you like always, but unlike previous incarnations, they don't sap your health slowly by latching on and gnawing at you while you're frozen... instead, they hurt you in one go with a swing of a heavy cleaver-like blade. Big Creepy-Crawlies:Tears of the Kingdomgives Gibdos notably insectoid characteristics.

characters.name: Goriyas
characters.description: Demons that resemble anthropomorphic Scottish terriers. They are known for using boomerangs. To date, they have only appeared in the 2D top-down games. A different creature with a ratlike appearance and the ability to shoot fireballs, calledCopi, wasrenamedGoriya overseas, but in Japan is separate from Goriya. Animal Facial Hair: Particularly noticeable inAdventure of Link, Goriyas have long and well-done mustaches much like a Scottish terrier. Battle Boomerang: Their weapons in all games. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome: Despite being quite prominent among Ganon's minions in the first two games and receiving dialogue, they pretty much just disappeared afterwards aside from a few minor cameos. Composite Character: Overseas material attempts to claim thatCopisare actually Goriyas.

characters.name: Guays
characters.description: Large black birds that circle above Link's reach and home in on him when he comes close. The Bus Came Back: They reappear inThe Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom, having a design that resembles theirOcarina of Time/Majora's Maskappearance, but with more detailed wings akin to theirSkyward Swordincarnation. For added bonus points, they're in the same game as the Crows. Creepy Crows: More violently aggressive than creepyper se, but they have a distinctly corvid look to them and in many translations they're specifically named after crows. TheirOcarina of Time/Majora's Maskappearance has them resemble Black Plague Doctors, while theirTwilight Princessdesign has them withCreepy Blue Eyesand a more fitting creepy appearance. Dung Fu: InSkyward Sword, they attack by crapping on Link's head. Feathered Fiend: Large and aggressive birds that will attack Link on sight.

characters.name: Gyorgs
characters.description: Aggressive purple fishes with armored heads found in marine areas. Gyorg first appears as a unique boss inMajora's Mask, while common enemies by the same name are found inThe Wind Waker,Phantom Hourglass, andSpirit Tracks. Adaptation Species Change: The first Gyorg fromMajora's Maskresembled a bony fish like a piranha. The Gyorgs fromThe Wind Waker,Phantom Hourglass, andSpirit Tracksare instead sharks. And the Gyorgs fromThe Minish Capare rays. The Artifact: The original Gyorg was one of the Four Masked Beasts that Link must fight in a game that heavily focuses on masks as both collectible items and a general story motif, so it's understandable that it would have a bony mask on its face. The shark Gyorgs from the Toon Link games still have bony mask-like protrusions despite those games not having the same focus on masks. Degraded Boss: InMajora's MaskandThe Minish Cap, Gyorg is a unique boss. In the Toon Link games, Gyorgs are commonplace enemies of limited scope. Fiendish Fish: In all incarnations, Gyorgs are large, very aggressive fishes provided with armored heads and very large teeth.

characters.name: Helmasaurs
characters.description: Aggressive beasts that wear metal masks. The mask can be removed or destroyed to make them vulnerable. Attack Its Weak Point: If you can't remove the mask, target its unprotected back. Big Creepy-Crawlies: InMajora's Mask, they appear as insectoid monsters but otherwise act the same. In the English localization, theyretain their Japanese name "Hiploop", likely because the "Helmasaur" name wouldn't make sense for them there. Cool Mask: It can be removed or destroyed to make them more vulnerable. In some games, their face underneath is surprisingly cute. Dash Attack: Their primary move is to charge at Link head-on.

characters.name: Hinox
characters.description: Giant, powerfulone-eyedogres that debuted in aA Link to the Past. They typically attack Link with bombs. Attack Its Weak Point: InPhantom Hourglass,Breath of the Wild, andTears of the Kingdom, youGo for the Eye, and in the latter games they'll try to cover it up after taking enough damage that way. Big Eater: InBreath of the WildandTears of the Kingdom, they'll drop lots of food items upon being killed; red ones drop fruit, blue ones roasted seafood, and black ones roasted meat. Whilst fighting Link, they also clearly intend to eat him. Classical Cyclops: Hulking, aggressive giants with a single eye in the middle of their faces. Giant Mook: InBreath of the WildandTears of the Kingdom, they're slightly redesigned to resemble giant one-eyed Bokoblins.

characters.name: Hoarders
characters.description: Hermit crab-like creatures that hide beneath rocks and bushes and flee when Link approaches them. They appear exclusively in early 2D titles;The Minish Capmarks their last appearance outside of remakes, untilEchoes of Wisdom. Ambushing Enemy: They hide under pieces of the scenery, looking for all the world like perfectly normal rocks or bushes until they start moving. The Bus Came Back: They reappear inThe Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom, a wholetwenty yearssinceThe Minish Cap. Cowardly Mooks: When Link comes too close to them or removes their cover, they will run around in a panic and only settle down after a while if Link isn't close by — if they do bump into and damage him, it's only through sheer chance as they flee randomly around the area. Harmless Enemy: InA Link to the Past, they can't cause damage — they will only scurry in panic if approached, and if they bump into Link they will only knock him back. This is averted in later games, where they damage him on contact like other enemies.

characters.name: Keese
characters.description: Bat-like enemies that have appeared in every game since the original. They reside in dungeons or dark places and tend to swoop down upon Link, but they're usually not much of a threat, even in large numbers. They can come in fire or ice variations; they're still not much more of a threat, but they're bigger nuisances, as they can respectively burn your shield or freeze you solid. Asteroids Monster: Vires, large humanoid bats from the early games, split into two Keese after being killed. Bat Out of Hell: Outsized, hostile bats that attack Link on sight. Bat People: Vires are enemies resembling humanoid bats with separate arms and wings. They're a stronger variant of the common, entirely batlike Keese, and split into multiple Keese when killed.Zelda II: The Adventure of Linkhas Achemen, one-game enemies that resemble Vires in almost all respects save that they hang from ceilings to ambush Link. Call a Rabbit a "Smeerp": There's hardly any difference between Keese and bats. InBreath of the WildandTears of the Kingdom, they're slightly redesigned to look more monstrous.

characters.name: Lanmolas and Moldorms
characters.description: Two worm (or centipede) monsters. Lanmola usually has a vulnerable point on its head and it's often fought in a desert arena where it pops out of the sand, while Moldorm's weak spot is usually in the rear segment and it's often fought on high platforms, where it's easy to fall off to a lower room. Airborne Mook: Skytails — "tail" is the Japanese name for most versions of Moldorm — are winged, wormlike enemies with vulnerable tails that can be found flying around Thunderhead inSkyward Sword. Attack Its Weak Point: The giant versions have weaknesses at one end (head for Lanmola, tail for Moldorm). Cyclops: The Lanmolas in the original game had a single gigantic eye dominating its forehead. Degraded Boss: Moldorms have a tendency to zigzag between being weak, common enemies and unique bosses.

characters.name: Leevers
characters.description: Bizarre, whirling creatures found in beaches and deserts, Leevers emerge from the sand when Link comes close in order to attack him. Bizarre Alien Biology: They're gumdrop-shaped masses of flesh with blade-like growths projecting from their tops that drain energy from those they touch; in the early 2D titles, they're barely distinguishable as living beings and if anything look more like Blade Traps than organic creatures. In later games, they become more visually complex but still very alien beings, with areas on their bodies that suggest the presence of organs or sensory areas but which don't match up with real-life biology in any real way. Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: Some games have Leevers in different colors, such as Blue Leevers. Energy Absorption: The game manuals of the early games state that Leevers attack by draining energy from their victims. "Get Back Here!" Boss: They have a habit of making themselves impossible to harm, making Link wait for them to make themselves vulnerable, typically by diving beneath the sand between attacks.

characters.name: Like Likes
characters.description: Stomach-like blob monsters that swallow Link and devour certain items of his (usually shields). Decomposite Character: The "Pikit" enemy fromA Link to the Pastwas called a Like-Like in Japanese, but "normal" Like-Likes are added to the the GBA version. Elemental Powers: InTears of the Kingdom, there are Likes Likes with elemental powers like the Ice Like, the Shock Like, and the Fire Like. Each spit projectiles of their respective element. Evil Lawyer Joke: Although not referring to lawyers, the EnglishSuper Smash Bros. Meleesays that Like Likes get their name from an old Hylian proverb: "Shield-eaters and world leaders have many likes alike".Whatever that means. Feed It a Bomb: The Deku Like enemies inTwilight Princessserve as obstructions that cannot be destroyed unless they swallow a bomb. This is also a method to defeat Like Likes inPhantom Hourglass,Spirit Tracks, andTears of the Kingdom.

characters.name: Lizalfos and Dinolfos
characters.description: Lizard warriors that normally attack in pairs. Dinolfos are stronger and faster than the standard Lizalfos. Similar enemies invery early gamesare the Geru, Daira, and Zazak. Airborne Mook: Aeralfos, Lizalfos-like enemies with wings, fly around too high for Link's attacks to reach, even with arrows. InTwilight Princess, the player can deal with this by waiting for them to dive and using the Clawshot to grab their shield and drag them to the ground, while inTri Force Heroestheir backs can be attacked after a dive. Beware My Stinger Tail: It's not unheard of for Lizalfos to tie weapons to their tails, which they use to swipe at Link during combat. The ones inTwilight Princessuse axe blades in this manner, while the ones inSkyward Swordtip theirs with spiked maces. Breath Weapon: They sometimes have the ability to breathe fire. The ability was originally exclusive to Dinolfos inMajora's Mask, but has been given to Lizalfos fromSkyward Swordonward; there, Dark Lizalfos instead breathe a cloud of gas that incapacitates Link. Some Lizalfos inBreath of the WildandTears of the Kingdomcan also breathe ice or fire. Chuck Cunningham Syndrome:Daira haven't been seen in the main seriesAdventure of Link, thoughCadence of Hyrulebrought them back as minibosses.Geru entirely disappear afterAdventure of Linkwithout even spinoff appearances, no doubt because Lizalfos are basically the same thing.

characters.name: Lynels
characters.description: A group of well-armed and powerful centaurs with leonine features, comprising some of the toughest enemies Link can find. Breath Weapon: Some can breathe fire. Depending on the Artist: Not as extreme as many otherZeldamonsters like Moblins, but sometimes the lower body of a Lynel is based off a lion complete with paws rather than a horse as in the Game Boy games. Elite Mooks: High health, high strength, and very tenacious; the Lynels are some of the strongest non-boss enemies in the games they appear in. Expy: As lion-headed centaur creatures, they are very similar to the wemics fromDungeons & Dragons.

characters.name: Mothulas
characters.description: Moth-like enemies that often attack by spawning weaker foes. Airborne Mook: Mothulas come in winged and wingless variants inThe Wind Waker, making the winged kind fit this trope. Link can clip off their wings with ranged weapons, turning them into the flightless variety. Asteroids Monster: The Mothula boss in the Game Boy Advance remake ofA Link to the Pastcan create copies of itself that, when destroyed, split into four bees that chase after Link. The Bus Came Back: They reappear inEchoes of Wisdomafter being absent sinceSpirit Tracks. Cyclops: Mothulas have had a single eye in the middle of their foreheads sinceOracle of Seasons, much like other arthropod enemies like Gohmas and Tektites, thoughEchoes of Wisombrings back the two eyes.

characters.name: Octoroks
characters.description: An octopus (or squid in some cases) monster that shoots rocks from its snout. Notable for appearing in every singleZeldagame, with the exception ofTwilight Princess, in which they're replaced by aSuspiciously Similar Substitute, Toadpoli. Airborne Mook: Flying variants appear from time to time.Sky Octoroks appear inSkyward SwordandBreath of the Wild. The ones in the former fly through leaves attached to their tops, which they spin like propellers. The ones in the latter game are insteadLiving Gasbagsthat fly thanks to inflated mantles.Link's Awakeningfeatures Winged Octoroks that dodge Link's attacks by fluttering out of the way. Sky Octoroks appear inSkyward SwordandBreath of the Wild. The ones in the former fly through leaves attached to their tops, which they spin like propellers. The ones in the latter game are insteadLiving Gasbagsthat fly thanks to inflated mantles. Link's Awakeningfeatures Winged Octoroks that dodge Link's attacks by fluttering out of the way. Ambushing Enemy: InSkyward Sword,Breath of the Wild, andTears of the Kingdom, Octoroks disguise themselves as part of the scenery — exactly what they pretend to be (grass, shrubs, rocks, etc.) varies between environments — and pop out of the ground to attack when Link passes by.

characters.name: Peahats
characters.description: Flying plant roots that attack with sharp leaves. The Bus Came Back: They reappear inEchoes of Wisdomafter being absent sinceA Link Between Worlds. "Get Back Here!" Boss: They have a habit of making themselves impossible to harm, making Link wait for them to make themselves vulnerable. Peahats are notable in that they tend toflipfrom game to game whether they're vulnerable in their stationary state or their mobile state. Giant Mook: InOcarina of TimeandMajora's Mask, Peahats are big and can kill Link in Hyrule Field should he make the mistake of attacking one. Harmless Enemy: InTwilight PrincessandSkyward Sword, Peahats cannot harm Link in any way — in essence, they serve entirely as floating supports for grappling onto with the Clawshot.

characters.name: Phantoms
characters.description: Appearing inThe Legend of Zelda: Phantom HourglassandThe Legend of Zelda: Spirit Tracks, Phantoms are large, armor-clad monsters with an array of supernatural powers. BFS: They're usually seen wielding gigantic swords one-handed. Gold Phantoms wield axes just as effortlessly. Breakout Mook Character: They've become this to a degree. Back inPhantom Hourglass, they're just really powerful enemies from a single dungeon that you have to run away from. InSpirit Tracks, Zelda can possess them and you can switch between playing as Link and her via the Phantoms. Then they were added to Zelda'sSuper Smash Bros.moveset inSuper Smash Bros. for Nintendo 3DS and Wii U. Then they were possessed by Toon Zelda again for their playable appearance inHyrule Warriors. By this point, they've become synonymous with Zelda in terms of gameplay, even though she never directly encountered them in their debut game! Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: InPhantom Hourglass, Standard Phantoms wear blue, Swift Phantoms wear red, and Golden Phantoms wear gold. InSpirit Tracks, Standard Phantoms wear green, Torch Phantoms wear red, Warp Phantoms wear cyan, and Wrecker Phantoms wear black. Whenever Zelda takes over a Phantom, it's armor turns tan and purple. Hive Mind: InPhantom Hourglass, each Phantom is controlled by Bellum.

characters.name: Pols Voice
characters.description: Bizarre, vaguely rabbit-like creatures weak to sound and impervious to most other things, Pols Voices appear in dungeons in the originalThe Legend of Zelda I,The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakeningand the Oracle games. They disappear in later installments, but make a comeback inThe Legend of Zelda: Phantom Hourglass. Achilles' Heel: Even when immune to anything else, they're extremely sensitive to sound, and loud noises can stun them or kill them outright. The Cameo: A Pols Voice in itsLink's Awakening Switchdesign appears as a plush toy doll inThe Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom. Lamprey Mouth: InPhantom Hourglass, the bottom of their bodies consist entirely of giant, round, fang-lined mouths. Our Ghosts Are Different: According to the first game's manual, these bizarre large-eared hopping things are in fact ghosts.

characters.name: Rat
characters.description: Mouse-like enemies that inhabit dungeons and dirty places. Bandit Mook: InThe Wind Waker, they'll steal Link's Rupees if he drops them. Fantastic Fauna Counterpart:The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worldsintroduces the Dark Rats, their stronger Lorulean counterparts. The Goomba: One of the weakest enemies in the game, they can easily be dispatched with a simple sword swing or any weapon. An Ice Person:The Legend of Zelda: Tri Force Heroesintroduces the Blue Rats, which hide inside Snowballs until the Links destroy them, but otherwise act the same.

characters.name: River Zora
characters.description: Water-dwelling merfolk known to spit fireballs at anyone who trespasses their territories, not to be confused with their sleeker Sea Zora cousins. Black Bead Eyes: They sport these inEchoes of Wisdom, suitably making them look much less hostile. Breath Weapon:Fireballs; they're basically fire-breathing fish-men. Decomposite Character: It initially seemed that these Zora underwent aHeel–Race TurninOcarina of Time(or that they went through aFace–Heel TurnafterOcarina of Time, given that their enemy roles were in games that took place after it), butOracle of Agesestablished that the ugly enemy Zora are actually a separate race from the friendly humanoid Zora. Evil Counterpart Race:Oracle of Agesestablish the River Zoras as enemies to both the Hylians and friendly "Sea Zoras".Echoes of Wisdomdrops the "evil" part by showing both kinds of Zoras peacefully coexisting, with the closest thing to any antagonistic sentiment being an unrelated personal squabble between their leaders.

characters.name: Ropes
characters.description: Aggressive snakes found in dungeons throughout the series. Call a Rabbit a "Smeerp": Name aside, they're perfectly ordinary snakes. Elite Mook: Two kinds.Flashing Ropes appear in the second quest inThe Legend of Zelda 1. They become a lot more durable, although their attack stays the same.Golden Ropes inThe Minish Cap, a gold-colored variant that moves faster, deals more damage and has higher health. Flashing Ropes appear in the second quest inThe Legend of Zelda 1. They become a lot more durable, although their attack stays the same. Golden Ropes inThe Minish Cap, a gold-colored variant that moves faster, deals more damage and has higher health.

characters.name: Skullfish
characters.description: Skeletal fishes found in certain aquatic areas. Aquatic Mook: They're only found in watery areas, where they patrol waterways and attack Link when he wades or swims in. Dem Bones: They're for the most part entirely skeletal.Twilight Princessdownplays this; its version is still chiefly skeletal, but retains a cluster of red organs in its ribcage. Fiendish Fish: Monstrous, fanged undead husks of fish that attack Link on sight. Raising the Steaks: Undead fish.

characters.name: Skull Kids
characters.description: Mischievous scarecrow-like imps who inhabit the Lost Woods, said to be what happens when kids get lost in the forest. They're distinguished by having a flute-like instrument that can double as a blow dart shooter. One particular Skull Kid became a major antagonist inThe Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask. Adult Hater: InOcarina of Time, the Skull Kid will react with hostility if you meet him again as an adult, firing needles at you from his flute. The Ageless: Much like the Kokiri, they look and act like children, but are implied to be much, much older than they appear, with theMajora's MaskSkull Kid in particular having been friends with the Four Giantsbeforethey created Termina. Blackface-Style Caricature: All versions of the original Nintendo 64 release ofOcarina of Timeand the Japanese release ofMajora's Maskmade them resemble this, with dark faces and yellow lips. The international versions ofMajora's Maskand the 3DS re-releases of both games instead gave them wooden, scarecrow-like faces with some shadow effects and beaks instead of lips, whileTwilight Princesswent with more of a pale ghoulish design. Dub Name Change: They're called Stalkids in Japanese, explicitly tying them into the larger Stalfos family of monsters. Additionally, the German dubs rename them to Horrorkinder ("Horror Children") and the Italian ones to Bambini Perduti ("Lost Children").

characters.name: Skulltulas
characters.description: Armored spider monsters with a skull motif on the back. A smaller variant called Walltulas clings to vines that Link must climb, and must be snuck past or defeated from a distance if Link is to pass. All Webbed Up: While they have always had the ability to drop down from silk threads, their appearance inSkyward Swordhas them prepare whole webs to trap Link. Rarely, they can also shoot silk at Link to immobilize him. Ambushing Enemy: In most games, they hang from the ceiling and try to ambush Link by dropping on him when he passes beneath them. Art Evolution: Initially, Walltulas almost looked the same as Skulltulas during theN64games, but inTwilight Princess, as well asSkyward Sword, they have a different appearance, with the former being purple and red, while the latter has them be white with purple legs. Attack Its Weak Point: In theN64games andSkyward Sword, they can only be damaged by hitting their soft undersides.

characters.name: Stalfos
characters.description: Reanimated skeleton soldiers. If you count the Stalchildren and Ikana Guards inMajora's Maskand the Stal-enemies in the Wild Saga, these enemies have appeared in pretty much all the games in the series, save forEchoes of Wisdom. All There in the Manual: The official Nintendo guide forMajora's Maskconfirms the knights of Ikana are Stalfos.Hyrule Encyclopediaclaims that the Hero's Shade (the Hero of Time, who teaches his techniques to his descendant inTwilight Princess) is one, though this contradicts the game and other material. Ambiguously Human: The earlyZeldagames implied that they were reanimated human/Hylian skeletons, withOcarina of Timeexplicitly saying they're the result of adult Hylians getting lost inThe Lost Woods. Starting withThe Wind Waker's depiction of them with equine skulls, though, they have often been portrayed with unusual features like hornlike protrusions,Third Eyes, andextra arms, implying that they were always monsters even before losing their flesh.Breath of the WildandTears of the Kingdomgo further by featuring explicit Stal-versions of the common monsters rather than unique Stal-enemies. Ballistic Bone: Some variants such as Blue Stalfos and Red Stalfos throw them at you. These variants also have a nasty habit of jumping out of the way when you attack them with your sword. Dem Bones: They're theZeldaequivalent of the common "animated skeleton" you tend to see in fantasy settings.

characters.name: Tektites
characters.description: Four-legged arthropods that get around by hopping. Cyclops: They have a single eye, a trait shared with Gohmas and later, Mothulas. Four-Legged Insect: Arachnid, in this case. Tektites stand out as there are several other spider-like monsters which do have eight legs, such as some variants of Gohma and Skulltulas. Giant Spider: In the 3D games, they tend to resemble four-legged spiders around Link's size. In a Single Bound: They move by jumping very high.

characters.name: Wallmasters and Floormasters
characters.description: Disembodied giant hands that like to send Link back to the dungeon's entrance (or a cell, in some cases). Wallmasters emerge from walls or drop down from the ceiling, while Floormasters emerge from the ground. Adaptational Late Appearance: Appears in the Switch remake forThe Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakeningas a Dungeon effect, despite Wallmasters themselves not appearing in the original game nor its DX remake. Ambushing Enemy: In some games, Wallmasters hide on ceilings, visible only by their shadow, and snatch you if you pass beneath them. Floormasters sometimes hide within floors (as inThe Legend of Zelda: The Wind Waker) or become invisible (a few do this inThe Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time) to ambush Link. However, in several other games, both enemies are often merelyMook Bouncersthat move around normally and quite visibly. Animate Body Parts: Living, disembodied hands that attack by grabbing at Link. Artifact Name: The originalThe Legend of Zelda Iis the only game in which Wallmasters actually come from the walls; in later games, they fall from the ceiling. This is averted in Japanese, where they're called Fallmasters fromA Link to the Pastonward.

characters.name: Wizzrobes
characters.description: Wizard-like, often avian enemies that attack with spells. Bird People: Their original art had a hooked nose that looked suspiciously like a beak when brightened, and several later games interpret them as straight-up humanoid birds. The Wizzrobes fromThe Wind Wakerare outright giant toucans withwinged arms, while the Wizzrobes inPhantom Hourglassresemble Black Plague Doctors. Boss in Mook Clothing: Easily the most dangerous regular enemies in the series besides Darknuts. They're minibosses inMajora's Maskand their figurine inWind Wakeris in the Nintendo Gallery's boss/strong-monster room. By the Lights of Their Eyes: In the earlier games, Wizzrobes were depicted with darkness where their faces should be, with only two glowing eyes visible. This design is subtly referenced byBreath of the WildandTears of the Kingdom, who, even though they have visible faces, are a rather dark grey color so their eyes shine through from a distance. Color-Coded Wizardry: Typically fromFour Swordsonwards, green-robed ones shoot basic energy projectiles, red-robed ones shoot fireballs and blue-robed ones shoot ice.Breath of the Wilddrops the green kind and adds yellow-robed ones that shoot lightning. Prior to that, there were just Blue and Red Wizzrobes, which reappear in theOraclegames as stronger variants to the usual green-robed kind.

characters.name: Wolfos
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Shift: Inverted afterMajora's Mask. In their first two appearances, they're somewhat anthropomorphicwolf men, but their appearance inTwilight Princess,Spirit Tracks,Cadence of Hyrule, andEchoes of Wisdomhave them look and act more like real wolves. Artifact Name:Their name has the "-fos" suffix that generally denotes the more humanoid monsters. This made sense in theN64games where they were more anthropomorphic, but less so where their later appearance has changed to look like natural wolves.White Wolfos were originally named that to distinguish them from their basic grey kin. They retain their full name inTwilight PrincessandSpirit Tracks, despite being the only kind of Wolfos encountered there. Their name has the "-fos" suffix that generally denotes the more humanoid monsters. This made sense in theN64games where they were more anthropomorphic, but less so where their later appearance has changed to look like natural wolves. White Wolfos were originally named that to distinguish them from their basic grey kin. They retain their full name inTwilight PrincessandSpirit Tracks, despite being the only kind of Wolfos encountered there. Attack Its Weak Point: Attacking one's tail will do more damage to it. If you're lucky enough to land a jump attack on it, this willOne-Hit Killthe beast.

characters.name: Zols and Gels
characters.description: Hopping, slime-like creatures found in dungeons. Zols are larger, and split into smaller Gels when killed.Zols and Gels are common enemies in the early games, but as the series went on they were eventually replaced by the Chuchus, though it didn't stop the Gels from being in the same game with them duringPhantom Hourglass. Asteroids Monster: Zols split into two Gels when defeated, although a powerful enough attack (such as a Bomb or a Spin Attack) will kill them outright and bypass the Gel stage. Blob Monster: They're small, rounded, hopping balls of slime that split into smaller copies of themselves when killed. The first game's manual leans into this trope more heavily than later depictions, showing Zols and Gels as much more slimy, dripping, messy things. The Bus Came Back: Zols reappear inThe Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom, which introduces 2 newvariantsin the form of Ignizol, which has a flame on its head like a candle, while Hydrozol is a light blue variant that looks like a water balloon. Colour-Coded for Your Convenience: Zols tend to come in distinct colored versions in games they appear in, although the precise meaning of each color varies from game to game.InA Link to the Past, Red Zols are the weakest, while Green and Yellow Zols are stronger and take more damage to defat.InLink's Awakeningand theOraclegames, Green Zols will not split into Gels when they die, while red ones will.

characters.name: The Hylians
characters.description: A tribe of pointy-eared humans responsible for the founding of Hyrule. In some games, all ordinary humans are Hylians, while in others round-eared humans are more common. Link and Zelda are always incarnated as Hylians. (Note that while Hylians are Hyruleans, the term "Hyrulean" refers toanyrace inhabiting Hyrule, including the clearly non-human ones.) Ambiguously Human: Depending on the origin story, they are either descended from the bird-likeOoccaor the dragon-likeZonai(with the latter theory offered as an explanation for their long ears). What either theory means for the Hylians' relationship to the otherwise normal "round-eared humans" is unknown. Arbitrary Skepticism: In some games, certain Hylians don't believe in their existence of magic despite the strangeness of their world. After clearing the Shadow Temple, a red-clothed man laughs at the claims of a blue-clothed man for telling him he saw Link teleport. The Chosen People: They are the chosen people of Hylia. Their pointy ears are said to allow them to listen to the Goddess. Divine Right of Kings: Hylians are the dominant race of Hyrule due to being the chosen people of the Goddess Hylia.

characters.name: The Kokiri/Koroks
characters.description: The Kokiri are the children of the forest who are under the protection of the Great Deku Tree. They resemble Hylian children, but never age. They eventually became the Koroks, an adorably quirky race ofPlant People. They're associated with the Goddess Farore. Anthropomorphic Shift: Drastically inverted. In their first appearance, they looked like Hylian children so Link could blend in. In all future appearances, they've essentially become living hunks of wood.Word of Godis that they are indeed the same race, despite the rename. Cheerful Child: The Kokiri are presented as an entire race of eternal children, and mostly are portrayed as cheerful, friendly and welcoming — saving individual jerks like Mido. The Koroks have the same attitude, but are much more inhuman-looking. Cloud Cuckoo Lander: Most of the Koroks are a little strange and a little air-headed. Creepy Child: The Kokiri are normallythe exact opposite of this, but at the end of the day, they are stillThe Fair Folk, and in some cases they can get very creepy indeed — such as the way one of themnonchalantly explainshow the Lost Woodstransforms any human who enters it into aStalfos.

characters.name: The Gorons
characters.description: A race who appear to be living boulders. They eat rocks and are usually found around volcanoes and mountains. They're usually associated with the Goddess Din. They're notable for being one of the most commonly appearing races, having shown up in every game since they were introduced inOcarina of Timeexcept forFour SwordsandTri Force Heroes. Big Fun: Big, rotund, boulder-like folk who are culturally predisposed to be boisterous and friendly with everyone. Bilingual Bonus: In a bit of aStealth Pun, they are named after the Japanese onomatopoeia for rolling rocks. Bizarre Alien Reproduction: A sidequest inTears of the Kingdomreveals that Gorons don't reproduce in any traditional sense. Instead, they're literally born from the land and refer to other Gorons born in the same place as them as their brothers. Bizarre Alien Locomotion: Gorons have short and stubby legs that, while very strong, don't allow them to run very fast. So to get places, they curl up and roll. They can pick up speed even uphill and on soft surfaces, and the fastest ones can match a horse in speed.

characters.name: The Sea Zoras
characters.description: A race of fish people, related to the enemy River Zoras. They're associated with the Goddess Nayru. Accessory-Wearing Cartoon Animal: The Zoras inTwilight Princess,Breath of the Wild, andTears of the Kingdomare shown sporting earrings, bracelets, anklets, necklaces, sashes, etc., but are otherwise unclothed. Adipose Rex: The Zora King tends to be significantly larger and heavier than his subjects. Alien Hair: They've got head appendages resembling the body of a fish, with the tail and pectoral fin portions positioned to resemble long hair and sideburns respectively. Amphibian at Large: Though they have traits of other sea animals on their bodies, inMajora's Maskwe see freshly-hatched infant Zora, who look like large Zora-colored tadpoles, implying that the race are biologically closer to amphibians than fish. Like most amphibians in the real world, the adults prefer to live around water but are perfectly capable of staying on land for long periods.

characters.name: The Gerudo
characters.description: An all-female desert people. It is said one male is born to their race every hundred years; this is where Ganon's most recognizable human form, Ganondorf, comes from. Animal Motifs: InSkyward Sword, the earliest game chronologically (and set before the first appearance of the Gerudo tribe), there is an insect located in the Lanayru Desert called the "Gerudo Dragonfly." Coupled with the Gerudo emblem resembling a dragonfly's head, it's implied the tribe is named after the insect. Amazon Brigade: The entire race is female, and they're all badasses. Amazonian Beauty: Gerudo are larger than other humans (seven-to-eight feet tall on average as adults) and tend to be naturally quite muscular. They're considered extremely attractive by Hylian men, to the point where it's common for men to risk capture trying to sneak into their towns. Bedlah Babe: Their default outfit, as shown in the picture to the right, is a vaguely Middle Eastern-looking apparel of a midriff-baring top and baggy-legged full-length trousers with pointy shoes. A veil is optional.

characters.name: The Sheikah
characters.description: The shadow people, sworn to protect the Hylians and the incarnations of Link and Zelda in each generation. They technically first appeared in the manual for the firstZeldagame before an in-game appearance inOcarina of Timeexclusively due to Impa. However, the Sheikah would not be seen in whole untilBreath of the Wild. A rogue sect called the Yiga Clan formed sometime beforeBreath of the Wild. According to the character compendium inTears of the Kingdom, the Sheikah are a sub-race of Hylians. Characterization Marches On: In their (not counting manuals) debut inOcarina of Time, the Sheikah are treated with the same individuality as all the other races in the game, due to Impa being a member of theParty of Representatives. TheWildduologue would clarify that the Sheikah are simply a sub-race of Hylians, compared to the still human-looking but treated more uniquely Gerudo. Dark Is Not Evil: Despite their elemental affiliation and sinister-looking appearances, the Sheikah are mostly, with the exception of the villainous Yiga Clan, heroic defenders of Hyrule. Dying Race: In most games, there are only a handful of them left, and typically the only one who appears is a version of Impa. They are thriving again by the time ofBreath of the Wild.

characters.name: The Rito
characters.description: A race of bird people. InThe Wind Wakerthey are descended from the Zora, butBreath of the Wildlater shows the two races co-existing. Adults Are More Anthropomorphic: Inverted. The young Rito look more like theirWind Wakercounterparts, while the adults are now full-fledgedBird People. Anthropomorphic Shift: Inverted.Wind Waker's Rito look human with bird wings and beaks. The Rito inBreath of the Wildfully resemble humanoid birds. Bird People: Humanoids with bird-like features. Even more so inBreath of the Wild, where they are more bird-like and can resemble a variety of different birds. Canon Immigrant: Eiji Aonuma says that he based the Rito on the Watarara race that was depicted in a bonus story of theOcarina of Timemanga.

characters.name: Humans
characters.description: "Human" refers to both the species that Hylians, Gerudo, Sheikah, the Wind Tribe, and more belong to and the unnamed race of ordinary round-eared humans that occasionally appear in the series. They most commonly appear in lands outside of Hyrule such as Koholint Island and Hytopia, but it's not uncommon for them to appear in Hyrule as well. Elemental Nation: Harder to pin down than the other races, though the forest-dwelling Ordonians and sky-dwelling Wind Tribe seem to share an affinity forAir. Humans Are Average: Humans are physically identical to Hylians in every way except their ears. They can also learn magic, as shown by several incarnation of the Sages, Maple and her grandmother Syrup. The only difference is that Hylians cansupposedlyhear the voices of the gods. Humans Are Not the Dominant Species: Subverted; this seems to be the case as the pointy eared Hylians are usually the most prosperous race seen throughout the games. However, games like Oracle duology,Twilight Princess, andTri Force Heroesshow that this actually only in Hyrule proper; the majority population of the world as a whole seems to indeed be round-eared humans. We simply get a skewed view of their importance since most games center around Hyrule. Humans Are Warriors: InTwilight Princess, compared to the Hylians. During Zant's invasion, a troop of at least 30 heavily-armed Hylian soldiers could not stop a few Twilit Messengers from overrunning the throne room and slaughtering them all, and the soldiers shown later in the game are completeMiles Gloriosi. Meanwhile, Ordon Village - consisting entirely of round-eared humansand Link- puts up a surprising fight. Rusl was able to single-handedly defend his entire village of Ordon from blins despite being unarmored and equipped with nothing but a sword. When Wolf Link arrives, another Ordonian villager isquick to attack him with a summoned hawk, almost killing him.noteAnd if he so much as comes within 10 feet of thewoundedRusl, the latter will quickl

characters.name: The Deku
characters.description: Small wooden beings who can shoot nuts out of their mouths. They are sometimes depicted as enemies and are usually comedic relief characters found early in games. Bullet Seed: They can shoot Deku Nuts out their mouths. The Bus Came Back: The Deku made an extended hiatus from the games after 2004, where they were a major race inFour Swords Adventuresand Link could encounter Business Scrubs inThe Minish Cap, with their archetype seemingly having been replaced by the Koroks. They made a surprising return in 2024 inEchoes of Wisdom. Cloud Cuckoolander: They have generally been this sinceMajora's Mask. Heli-Critter: Business Scrubs can use their head leaves like propellers to fly, and can presumably launch from Deku Flowers like Link does in Deku form.

characters.name: Demons
characters.description: Evil beings who have frequently unleashed their wrath upon Hyrule, whether directly or by means of the lesser monsters they create. Some villains such as Ganon and Vaati are mortals who became demons upon gaining powerful magic, others such as Demise and Malladus were demons to begin with, and most of the other villains of the series are implied to be demons. The Blin race mentioned above is implied to be a type of demon as well, albeit weaker ones who serve the stronger demons as soldiers. Cast of Snowflakes: The most physiologically diverse of all depicted races, as no two major demon characters in the series are ever depicted with many meaningful physical similarities. The Corrupter:Villains such as Ganon and Majora have demonstrated the ability to turn good people to evil, sometimes to the point of turning those people into demons and monsters themselves. Even completely non-malicious demons like Batreaux are depicted as unwillingly emitting an evil aura capable of making friendly creatures such as Remlits aggressive.Encyclopediasays monsters like Octoroks, Stalfos, Deku Babas and Moblins are corrupted animals, corpses, plants and species respectively. Even completely non-malicious demons like Batreaux are depicted as unwillingly emitting an evil aura capable of making friendly creatures such as Remlits aggressive. Encyclopediasays monsters like Octoroks, Stalfos, Deku Babas and Moblins are corrupted animals, corpses, plants and species respectively.

characters.name: Fairies
characters.description: Magical beings of good who live in underground fountains. There are two types of fairies, the small normal ones and the larger and more humanoid "Great Fairies". Auto-Revive: In most games in which they can be captured, fairies will automatically revive Link should he ever fall in battle. Faerie Court: Depending on the game.A Link to the Past,Link's Awakening,Oracle of Ages, andThe Wind Wakerall feature designated Fairy Queens who are even more powerful than the Great Fairies.Ocarina of TimeandTwilight Princessalso feature Great Fairies who are identified as being the rulers or queens of the fairy race. Equipment Upgrade: The Great Fairies usually fill this role, enhancing the effectiveness or carrying capacity of Link's items or blessing him with magic spells and other abilities. Fairy Companion:Ocarina of Time,Majora's Mask, andPhantom Hourglasseach give Link a fairy guide to accompany him and provide exposition.
